transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, your clinical conversational agent. I'm calling to check in with you after your cataract surgery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, thanks for calling. I do have a few questions. When can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're looking to get back to gardening soon. According to the advice, you can start with light exercise, including gardening, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's a good idea to avoid heavy lifting or bending, and be gentle with your eyes. Also, remember to keep water away from your eyes, especially in the first month. Would you like to know about anything else?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's helpful, thank you. I was also wondering when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: If you were using eye drops before your operation, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. You can also get preservative-free eye drops from the pharmacist to help with dryness. It's recommended to use them four times daily to start. If you're running out, you can get more from your GP. Do you have any other questions about your eye drops or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the advice. I'm also experiencing a lot of sensitivity to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: Some sensitivity to light is normal, but if it's severe or causing you a lot of discomfort, we'd recommend taking some precautions. You can try wearing sunglasses when you're going outside to help block out the light. If the sensitivity is significant and you're also experiencing redness or pain in the eye, we may need to assess it further. Would you like to know more about managing sensitivity to light?
